newsitem.title: USA: Sears recalls 14,000 water filter cartridges.
newsitem.headline: Sears recalls 14,000 water filter cartridges.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck & Co. said Tuesday it was recalling about 14,000 Sears water filter cartridges used to filter drinking water because of possible nickel chloride contamination.

Sears said it was cooperating with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission and Ecodyne Water Systems, the distributor, to recall the cartridges sold under the name "Sears Chemical Contaminant/Taste and Odor Filter".
The filters fit most standard-sized under-sink and countertop water filters, and have been sold at Sears stores nationwide since March 1996 for about $17.

Sears said an incorrect form of carbon was used to make some of the filter cartridges. The carbon used contains nickel chloride, which releases nickel into the water and can be harmful if ingested. Nickel chloride can cause abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
"Although only a small amount may be affected, we are recalling all as a precautionary measure," Theresa Ferguson, spokeswoman for Sears, said in an interview.
Sears said it was not aware of any injuries involving the product. The recall is to prevent the possibility of injury, the company said.

Consumers who have used the affected filter cartridges and are displaying the symptoms should see a medical professional for possible ingestion of nickel. Pregnant women and dialysis patients who have consumed water from this filter should also advise their physicians.
Sears said pregnant women, dialysis patients, infants, small children, the elderly and people with kidney problems or a nickel allergy may be more sensitive to the effects of nickel chloride.

Sears said Ecodyne informed it of the problem on Feb. 21, and it immediately stopped sale of the cartridges. Cartridges containing nickel chloride, when initially used, cause the filtered water to taste metallic and turn green.
The filter is a cylinder-shaped cartridge with a white plastic casing and a 1.5-inch wide green end cap. It is the only Sears water filter with the green end cap, the company said.
Sears said the carbon for the cartridges was provided by Barneby & Sutcliffe, based in Ohio. The cartridges were manufactured by Ametek, based in Pennsylvania.
Consumers should immediately stop using the cartridge and call Ecodyne Water Systems at 800-945-0109 for instructions on returning it for a full refund or replacement.
No other Sears water filters are involved in the recall.
